rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the resulting mixture of substances.

example.english: This drink is a mix of milk and chocolate.
example.traditional: 呢杯飲品係牛奶同朱古力嘅混合物。
example.jyutping: ni1 bui1 jam2 ban2 hai6 ngau4 naai5 tung4 zyu1 gu1 lik6 ge3 wan6 hap6 mat6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for combining separate things together.

example.english: We’ll mix the people from the two teams together for the game.
example.traditional: 我哋將兩隊嘅人撈埋一齊玩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 zoeng1 loeng5 deoi6 ge3 jan4 lou1 maai4 jat1 cai4 waan2

rows.note: Use this for a packaged powder mix to which other ingredients are added, such as cake or pancake mix.

example.english: This cake mix can be made into a cake just by adding water.
example.traditional: 呢包預拌粉加水就可以整蛋糕。
example.jyutping: ni1 baau1 jyu6 bun6 fan2 gaa1 seoi2 zau6 ho2 ji5 zing2 daan6 gou1

rows.note: Use 撈 for stirring or mixing food ingredients together.

example.english: Before cooking the noodles, mix the vegetables and meat evenly.
example.traditional: 煮麵之前，先將啲菜同肉撈勻。
example.jyutping: zyu2 min6 zi1 cin4 sin1 zoeng1 di1 coi3 tung4 juk6 lou1 wan4

rows.note: Use 溝 especially when mixing liquids or adding one drink or liquid to another.

example.english: Don’t mix so much milk into the coffee.
example.jyutping: jam2 gaa3 fe1 m4 hou2 kau1 gam3 do1 naai5

rows.note: Use this formal or written verb for combining ingredients or separate things when colloquial 撈 or 撈埋 is less suitable.

example.english: The laboratory staff will mix the two solutions.
example.traditional: 實驗人員會將兩種溶液混合。
example.jyutping: sat6 jim6 jan4 jyun4 wui5 zoeng1 loeng5 zung2 jung4 jik6 wan6 hap6
